core_obligations: Get flatness and set the target: by the cited flatness permanence q is flat, so by the flat-fibres-characterisation of syntomicity it suffices to prove that the fibres of Y over S are local complete intersections (proof lines 3079-3081).

Reduce the base to a field: for a point s of S, the morphism between the fibres X_s to Y_s is a base change of the surjective syntomic f, hence surjective and syntomic, X_s is syntomic over the residue field and Y_s is locally of finite type over it; therefore one may assume that S is the spectrum of a field (proof lines 3082-3090).

Build the local algebra diagram: for a point y of Y choose affine opens Spec(A) in Y and Spec(B) in X with the image of Spec(B) inside Spec(A) and with a point x mapping to y, choose presentations of A and of B over the polynomial rings, and record the corresponding primes together with the resulting commutative diagram of local rings (proof lines 3091-3110).

Check the hypotheses of the cited permanence lemma and conclude: the two trivial conditions hold, flatness of X to Y gives the flatness condition, and the two local rings that must be complete intersections are the local ring of Y at y and the local ring of the fibre X_y at x, which are complete intersections because f and p are syntomic; the lemma then produces the conclusion that the local ring of Y at y is a complete intersection ring, which by the same-chapter characterisation makes Y syntomic over the field at y (proof lines 3111-3125).
proof_roadmap: Reduce syntomicity of q to the local complete intersection property of its fibres, using flatness permanence and the flat-fibres criterion (proof lines 3079-3081).

Reduce further to a field as base, then translate the local complete intersection property of the relevant local rings into the hypotheses of the cited algebra permanence lemma and apply it (proof lines 3082-3125).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the standard permanence statement for syntomic morphisms: in a commutative triangle with f surjective and syntomic, p syntomic and q locally of finite presentation, the morphism q is syntomic (statement lines 6057-6077). The counted proof has two distinct layers: it reduces the geometric statement to the local complete intersection property of the fibres of q using the flat-fibres criterion, and it reduces the base to the spectrum of a field using base change of syntomic and locally finite type morphisms (proof lines 3079-3090); then it sets up the commutative diagram of local rings attached to chosen affine charts and checks, one by one, the four hypotheses of the cited algebra permanence lemma, the third of which is that the local rings of the target and of the fibre are complete intersection rings (proof lines 3091-3125). It is H2: the deep permanence input is the cited algebra lemma, while the geometric reductions and the verification of its hypotheses are the author's own and are carried out inside the counted span.
